marks.gloss_en: כיוצא בה שמעתי, דתנן ... ודאי מקדח וחיסומו: Beit Shammai's drill is a hole the drill enters and leaves; so too the karshina (via p_karshina_kemakdeach)
Rav Huna Rabba's analogy: the karshina-measure is like Beit Shammai's drill-measure, which is a hole the drill enters and leaves
דתנן: כלי שנטמא אחוריו במשקין -- אחוריו טמאין... (kind tanya_kevatei for דתנן, under protest: no SupportKind names it)
for Torah impurity, indeed; here it speaks of rabbinic liquid-impurity (= p_okimta_tumat_mashkin), which the Rabbis made like earthenware (38a.10-11)
for Torah impurity, indeed so; here it speaks of the rabbinic impurity of liquids
אישתיק; Rav Chisda: perhaps 'a drill and its blockage' -- affirmed as certain by Rav Tachlifa (38a.2) (= p_makdeach_vechisumo)
Beit Shammai's 'drill-hole' is the drill with its blockage (a hole the drill enters and leaves) -- somewhat larger than a sela
the Neronian sela equals the large drill; a plain sela is smaller than a plain drill (= p_nachman_sela_neronit, p_nachman_sela_stam_zutra)
Rav Nachman: it is the NERONIAN sela that we learned to equal the large drill
כלי חרס, בתוכו תלה רחמנא -- with a receptacle it is defiled, without one it is not defiled at all!
הכי קאמר -- the counterpart among rinsable vessels (= p_ryba_kenegdo_bichli_shetef)
R' Yitzchak bar Avin: thus it says -- whatever has no receptacle among earthenware [is pure]; its counterpart among rinsable vessels has no division of back
בשלמא כלי חרס גלי ביה רחמנא תוכו, אלא כלי שטף -- מי גלי ביה רחמנא תוכו?
אי הכי, אין לו תוך נמי ליעביד נמי היכירא!
the Rabbis made a marker, so that teruma and kodashim not be burnt on its account
since a marker was made for the receptacle case, the no-receptacle case is known to be rabbinic (= p_yedia_ein_lo_toch_derabanan)
since they made a marker for the vessel with a receptacle, it is known that [the liquid-impurity of] one without a receptacle is rabbinic
ואין לו תוך בכלי שטף דאורייתא בר קבולי טומאה הוא? דומיא דשק בעינן -- as a sack is carried full and empty, so anything [susceptible] is carried full and empty
those fit for midras (= p_chazu_lemidrasot)
אי הכי, חרס נמי! -- earthenware fit for sitting should likewise be [decreed susceptible]
אין מדרס בכלי חרס (= p_ein_midras_bicheres)
[the receptacle-less rinsable vessels meant are] those fit for midras
הניחא לרבי מאיר, אלא לרבנן מאי איכא למימר? דתנן: Chachamim -- BS's drill is the large one of the chamber, so it again equals the sela -- unanswered
by inference, a plain drill [Beit Shammai's] is smaller than a sela
ולרבי מאיר מי ניחא? הוה ליה מקולי בית שמאי ומחומרי בית הלל -- a drill smaller than a sela makes BS lenient and BH stringent on the skull, and that is not on the list we learned -- unanswered
the leniencies of Beit Shammai and stringencies of Beit Hillel that we learned, we learned; those we did not learn, we did not learn
Rabban Gamliel HaZaken (via Chizkiya avi Ikkesh): whatever among earthenware has no receptacle has no division of back [from inside]: inside impure -- back impure, back impure -- inside impure
it teaches that a rinsable vessel WITH a receptacle is like earthenware: inside impure -- back impure; inside not impure -- back not impure
by Torah law neither food nor liquid defiles a vessel; the Rabbis decreed it on account of the liquids of a zav and zava
so the Rabbis made it like earthenware impurity, not like its own Torah impurity
Rav Pappa: [the drill equal to the sela, in the window mishna] is the LARGE drill that we learned
R' Meir: [Beit Shammai's drill] is the small drill of physicians
the ris of the eye that was pierced, damaged, or split [is a blemish]
